title: Psalms Chapter 81 Quiz - Multi-Level
description: An enhanced quiz on Psalms chapter 81 with Easy, Medium, Hard, and Theological levels. Each level has 15 carefully crafted questions. Choose your difficulty and dive in!

easy.title: Psalms Chapter 81 Quiz - Easy Level
easy.description: Perfect for beginners! Test your basic knowledge of Psalms Chapter 81.

questions.question: In Psalms 81, which of the following appears FIRST in the chapter?
options: Sing aloud unto God our strength
Blow up the trumpet in the new moon
This he ordained in Joseph for a testimony
Take a psalm, and bring hither the timbrel
questions.correctAnswer: Sing aloud unto God our strength
questions.explanation: The command to sing aloud unto God our strength appears first in Psalms 81:1.

questions.question: To whom is the Psalm directed in Psalms 81:1?
options: To the chief Musician upon Gittith
To the priests
To the people of Egypt
To the children of Israel
questions.correctAnswer: To the chief Musician upon Gittith
questions.explanation: The Psalm is directed to the chief Musician upon Gittith according to Psalms 81:1.

questions.question: What musical instruments are mentioned in Psalms 81:2?
options: Timbrel, harp, and psaltery
Trumpet, cymbals, and harp
Lyre, flute, and drum
Tambourine, horn, and harp
questions.correctAnswer: Timbrel, harp, and psaltery
questions.explanation: Psalms 81:2 mentions the timbrel, the pleasant harp, and the psaltery.

questions.question: When is the trumpet to be blown according to Psalms 81:3?
options: In the new moon and on our solemn feast day
At dawn and at dusk
During the harvest festival
At the end of the Sabbath
questions.correctAnswer: In the new moon and on our solemn feast day
questions.explanation: Psalms 81:3 states the trumpet should be blown in the new moon and on the solemn feast day.

questions.question: What was the statute mentioned in Psalms 81:4?
options: A statute for Israel and a law of the God of Jacob
A commandment for the priests
A tradition from Egypt
A rule for the kings of Israel
questions.correctAnswer: A statute for Israel and a law of the God of Jacob
questions.explanation: Psalms 81:4 states this was a statute for Israel and a law of the God of Jacob.

questions.question: In which land did God hear a language He understood not, according to Psalms 81:5?
options: Egypt
Canaan
Babylon
Assyria
questions.correctAnswer: Egypt
questions.explanation: Psalms 81:5 mentions God heard a language He understood not when He went through the land of Egypt.

questions.question: Who was the statute ordained in, as mentioned in Psalms 81:5?
options: Joseph
Moses
David
Aaron
questions.correctAnswer: Joseph
questions.explanation: Psalms 81:5 states the statute was ordained in Joseph for a testimony.

questions.question: What did God remove from the people according to Psalms 81:6?
options: His shoulder from the burden
The shackles from their feet
The blindness from their eyes
The chains from their hands
questions.correctAnswer: His shoulder from the burden
questions.explanation: Psalms 81:6 states God removed his shoulder from the burden.

questions.question: What were the hands delivered from, according to Psalms 81:6?
options: The pots
The chains
The yoke
The sword
questions.correctAnswer: The pots
questions.explanation: Psalms 81:6 says the hands were delivered from the pots.

questions.question: What kind of noise does Psalms 81:1 instruct to make unto God?
options: A joyful noise
A quiet whisper
A solemn chant
A mournful cry
questions.correctAnswer: A joyful noise
questions.explanation: Psalms 81:1 commands to make a joyful noise unto God.

questions.question: Who is referred to as 'God of Jacob' in Psalms 81?
options: God
Moses
Joseph
David
questions.correctAnswer: God
questions.explanation: Psalms 81:1 and 81:4 refer to God as the God of Jacob.

questions.question: True or False: Psalms 81 commands to blow the trumpet at the new moon.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Psalms 81:3 instructs to blow the trumpet in the new moon.

questions.question: True or False: Psalms 81 mentions that the statute was a law of the God of Jacob.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Psalms 81:4 states the statute was a law of the God of Jacob.

questions.question: True or False: Psalms 81 says that the people were commanded to fast during the new moon.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Psalms 81:3 mentions blowing the trumpet in the new moon but does not mention fasting.

questions.question: True or False: Psalms 81 states that the people were delivered from slavery by crossing the Red Sea.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Psalms 81:6 speaks of removing the burden and delivering hands from the pots but does not mention crossing the Red Sea.

medium.title: Psalms Chapter 81 Quiz - Medium Level
medium.description: Ready for more? Apply biblical truths from Psalms Chapter 81 to real-life situations.

questions.question: According to Psalms 81:7, where did God answer Israel when they called in trouble?
options: In the secret place of thunder
On the mountaintop
By the rivers of Babylon
In the valley of dry bones
questions.correctAnswer: In the secret place of thunder
questions.explanation: Psalms 81:7 explicitly states that God answered Israel in the secret place of thunder when they called in trouble.

questions.question: What does Psalms 81:10 promise will happen if someone hearkens to God as commanded in Psalms 81:8?
options: God will fill their mouth wide
They will be taken out of Egypt
They will conquer their enemies
They will never know trouble
questions.correctAnswer: God will fill their mouth wide
questions.explanation: Psalms 81:8 commands Israel to hearken to God, and Psalms 81:10 promises that if they do, God will open their mouth wide and fill it.

questions.question: What reason does Psalms 81:11 give for God giving up His people to their own desires?
options: Because they would not hearken to His voice
Because they worshipped strange gods
Because they forgot His statutes
Because they were proud and arrogant
questions.correctAnswer: Because they would not hearken to His voice
questions.explanation: Psalms 81:11 clearly states that God gave them up because His people would not hearken to His voice.

questions.question: How does Psalms 81:12 explain the result of Israel not hearkening to God as mentioned in Psalms 81:11?
options: They walked in their own counsels
They were punished by enemies
They returned to Egypt
They prospered in their land
questions.correctAnswer: They walked in their own counsels
questions.explanation: Psalms 81:12 follows Psalms 81:11 by stating that because Israel did not hearken, God gave them up to walk in their own counsels.

questions.question: What is the significance of the waters of Meribah mentioned in Psalms 81:7 for practical faith?
options: It represents God testing and proving His people’s trust
It symbolizes a place of healing and forgiveness
It is where the Israelites first worshiped God
It signifies the entrance to the Promised Land
questions.correctAnswer: It represents God testing and proving His people’s trust
questions.explanation: Psalms 81:7 mentions God proving Israel at the waters of Meribah, illustrating the testing of their faith and trust in Him.

questions.question: What does God command Israel regarding strange gods in Psalms 81:9?
options: There shall be no strange god in thee
You may worship any god you choose
Strange gods are tolerated if they bring peace
You should learn from strange gods
questions.correctAnswer: There shall be no strange god in thee
questions.explanation: Psalms 81:9 commands that no strange god should be in Israel and they should not worship any strange god.

questions.question: What practical lesson about obedience can be drawn from Psalms 81:12?
options: Disobedience leads to following one’s own misguided desires
Obedience guarantees earthly riches
God will always protect disobedient people
Ignoring God’s law has no real consequences
questions.correctAnswer: Disobedience leads to following one’s own misguided desires
questions.explanation: Psalms 81:12 explains that because Israel did not listen, God gave them up to their own hearts’ lust and counsels, showing the consequences of disobedience.

questions.question: In Psalms 81:10, what does God say He will do if Israel opens their mouth wide?
options: He will fill it
He will silence it
He will judge it
He will bless it with riches
questions.correctAnswer: He will fill it
questions.explanation: Psalms 81:10 states that if Israel opens their mouth wide, God will fill it, implying provision and blessing.

questions.question: How does the context of Psalms 81:1-6 enhance understanding of God’s relationship with Israel in Psalms 81:7-12?
options: It shows God’s past deliverance and care as foundation for calling Israel to obedience
It focuses on Israel’s conquest of Canaan
It describes the building of the temple
It explains the genealogy of Asaph
questions.correctAnswer: It shows God’s past deliverance and care as foundation for calling Israel to obedience
questions.explanation: Psalms 81:1-6 recount God’s deliverance from Egypt and provision, setting the stage for the call to obedience in verses 7-12.

questions.question: What does the phrase 'I removed his shoulder from the burden' in Psalms 81:6 imply for Christian living?
options: God relieves believers from heavy burdens and provides help
Believers must carry burdens alone
Only physical burdens are removed by God
God punishes those who complain
questions.correctAnswer: God relieves believers from heavy burdens and provides help
questions.explanation: Psalms 81:6 highlights God’s intervention in delivering Israel from burdens, encouraging believers to trust God for relief in trials.

questions.question: What practical warning does Psalms 81:11 offer for believers today?
options: Ignoring God’s voice leads to spiritual decline
God will always forgive immediately
It is acceptable to worship other gods
Obedience is optional in faith
questions.correctAnswer: Ignoring God’s voice leads to spiritual decline
questions.explanation: Psalms 81:11 warns that God’s people would not listen, which implies the danger of ignoring God’s guidance.

questions.question: How can Psalms 81:9 influence a believer’s attitude toward idolatry?
options: It commands total rejection of all strange gods
It permits some idolatry if done in secret
It suggests tolerance for cultural gods
It encourages learning from other religions
questions.correctAnswer: It commands total rejection of all strange gods
questions.explanation: Psalms 81:9 clearly states there shall be no strange god in Israel, directing believers to reject idolatry completely.

questions.question: What is the significance of the 'new moon' and 'solemn feast day' mentioned in Psalms 81:3 in relation to worship?
options: These are appointed times for joyful worship and remembrance
They are times for fasting and silence
They represent pagan festivals
They are optional celebrations
questions.correctAnswer: These are appointed times for joyful worship and remembrance
questions.explanation: Psalms 81:3 instructs Israel to blow the trumpet on the new moon and solemn feast day, highlighting the importance of set times for worship.

questions.question: True or False: Psalms 81:4 states that the laws given to Israel were merely suggestions and not mandatory.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Psalms 81:4 says the statute and law of God were appointed and binding for Israel, not mere suggestions.

questions.question: True or False: Psalms 81:5 refers to God hearing a language He understood not during Israel’s exodus.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Psalms 81:5 mentions God hearing a language He did not understand when Israel went out of Egypt, highlighting God’s awareness of their plight.

hard.title: Psalms Chapter 81 Quiz - Hard Level
hard.description: Challenge yourself with deep analysis and cross-biblical connections from Psalms Chapter 81.

questions.question: According to Psalms 81:13, what does the Psalmist lament about the people of Israel?
options: They had hearkened unto God and walked in His ways
They had forsaken their own ways for God's statutes
They had not hearkened unto God and had not walked in His ways
They had worshipped strange gods instead of God
questions.correctAnswer: They had not hearkened unto God and had not walked in His ways
questions.explanation: Psalms 81:13 states, "Oh that my people had hearkened unto me, and Israel had walked in my ways!" which expresses a lament that Israel did not listen or walk in God's ways.

questions.question: What consequence does Psalms 81:14 say would have occurred if Israel had walked in God's ways?
options: God would have given them abundant wealth
God would have subdued their enemies and turned His hand against adversaries
God would have made them rulers over other nations
God would have brought judgment upon their enemies
questions.correctAnswer: God would have subdued their enemies and turned His hand against adversaries
questions.explanation: Psalms 81:14 states, "I should soon have subdued their enemies, and turned my hand against their adversaries," indicating the protection and victory God would have granted.

questions.question: In Psalms 81:15, who should have submitted themselves unto the LORD?
options: The haters of the LORD
The people of Egypt
The leaders of Israel
The priests and Levites
questions.correctAnswer: The haters of the LORD
questions.explanation: Psalms 81:15 says, "The haters of the LORD should have submitted themselves unto him," showing that even those opposed to God would have been humbled.

questions.question: What imagery does Psalms 81:16 use to describe how God would have satisfied Israel?
options: With manna from heaven and water from the rock
With the finest of the wheat and honey out of the rock
With abundant livestock and flowing rivers
With gold and silver treasures
questions.correctAnswer: With the finest of the wheat and honey out of the rock
questions.explanation: Psalms 81:16 states, "He should have fed them also with the finest of the wheat: and with honey out of the rock should I have satisfied thee," using agricultural and natural imagery to depict God's provision.

questions.question: Which verse immediately follows the lament in Psalms 81:13 about Israel not hearkening?
options: Psalms 81:14 about subduing enemies
Psalms 81:15 about the haters submitting
Psalms 81:12 about walking in their own counsels
Psalms 81:16 about feeding with wheat and honey
questions.correctAnswer: Psalms 81:14 about subduing enemies
questions.explanation: Psalms 81:14 directly follows 81:13 and discusses how God would have subdued their enemies if Israel had walked in His ways.

questions.question: According to Psalms 81:13-16, which theme best summarizes this passage?
options: God’s judgment upon Israel for their rebellion
The blessings forfeited due to Israel’s disobedience
The call to worship with musical instruments
The historical exodus from Egypt
questions.correctAnswer: The blessings forfeited due to Israel’s disobedience
questions.explanation: The passage Psalms 81:13-16 laments Israel’s failure to heed God, highlighting the blessings and protection they missed out on, such as victory over enemies and provision with the finest wheat and honey.

questions.question: What does the Hebrew word 'hearkened' (שָׁמַע, shama) in Psalms 81:13 mean?
options: To listen attentively and obey
To speak loudly
To forget or ignore
To question or doubt
questions.correctAnswer: To listen attentively and obey
questions.explanation: The Hebrew root שָׁמַע (shama) commonly means to hear with the implication of obedience, as seen in Psalms 81:13 where God laments Israel did not 'hearken' unto Him.

questions.question: Which literary device is prominently used in Psalms 81:13-16, especially in contrasting Israel’s disobedience with God’s blessings?
options: Chiasmus
Alliteration
Simile
Hyperbole
questions.correctAnswer: Chiasmus
questions.explanation: Psalms 81:13-16 displays chiasmus, a literary device where ideas are presented and then mirrored in reverse order, contrasting Israel’s failure with the blessings they would have received.

questions.question: Which New Testament passage echoes the theme of God’s provision and care for His people found in Psalms 81:16?
options: John 6:35 - Jesus as the Bread of Life
Romans 5:8 - God’s love shown through Christ
Hebrews 11:1 - Faith as assurance
Acts 2:4 - The coming of the Holy Spirit
questions.correctAnswer: John 6:35 - Jesus as the Bread of Life
questions.explanation: John 6:35 where Jesus says, "I am the bread of life," connects to Psalms 81:16’s imagery of God feeding Israel with the finest wheat and honey, symbolizing divine provision.

questions.question: Which Old Testament passage connects with Psalms 81:7’s reference to the waters of Meribah where God tested Israel?
options: Exodus 17:1-7 - Water from the rock at Meribah
Genesis 12:1-3 - God’s covenant with Abram
Leviticus 23:4-8 - The appointed feasts
Numbers 13:25 - Spies sent into Canaan
questions.correctAnswer: Exodus 17:1-7 - Water from the rock at Meribah
questions.explanation: Psalms 81:7 references God proving Israel at the waters of Meribah, which is directly recounted in Exodus 17:1-7 where Moses strikes the rock to provide water.

questions.question: What comes immediately before the exhortation in Psalms 81:13 about Israel walking in God's ways?
options: God giving up Israel to their own hearts' lust (Psalms 81:12)
God promising to fill the mouth of Israel (Psalms 81:10)
A call to worship with the timbrel and harp (Psalms 81:2)
The prohibition of strange gods (Psalms 81:9)
questions.correctAnswer: God giving up Israel to their own hearts' lust (Psalms 81:12)
questions.explanation: Psalms 81:12 precedes verse 13 and explains that God gave Israel up to their own desires because they would not listen, setting the context for the lament in verse 13.

questions.question: Which type of parallelism is evident in Psalms 81:13-16 where the first half expresses a wish and the second half describes consequences?
options: Synthetic parallelism
Synonymous parallelism
Antithetic parallelism
Emblematic parallelism
questions.correctAnswer: Synthetic parallelism
questions.explanation: Psalms 81:13-16 shows synthetic parallelism where the second lines build upon or complete the idea of the first, e.g., Israel’s disobedience followed by what God would have done.

questions.question: How does Psalms 81:10 use typology to connect God’s deliverance of Israel with spiritual nourishment?
options: God as the provider who fills Israel’s mouth after the Exodus
The new moon festival as a symbol of renewal
The harp and timbrel representing joy in worship
The subduing of enemies as a messianic prophecy
questions.correctAnswer: God as the provider who fills Israel’s mouth after the Exodus
questions.explanation: Psalms 81:10 typologically links God’s deliverance from Egypt with His promise to fill Israel’s mouth, symbolizing spiritual provision following physical deliverance.

questions.question: Which statement is TRUE regarding the structure of Psalms 81 as seen in the chapter?
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: The Psalm begins with a call to worship (verses 1-5), recounts God's past deliverance (verses 6-7), calls for Israel to listen and obey (verses 8-12), and ends with a lament and promise of blessings if they obey (verses 13-16), showing a clear inclusio and chiastic arrangement (Psalms 81:1-16).

questions.question: The phrase 'honey out of the rock' in Psalms 81:16 is a common biblical metaphor for impossible provision.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: While 'honey out of the rock' in Psalms 81:16 is poetic imagery of abundant provision, it is not generally understood as impossible but rather miraculous sustenance, reflecting God's ability to provide in harsh conditions.

theological.title: Psalms Chapter 81 Quiz - Theological Level
theological.description: Deep biblical theology from Psalms Chapter 81 that unites all believers. Explore foundational truths about God, creation, and humanity.

questions.question: What doctrine does Psalms 81:10 teach about God's provision for His people?
options: God promises to satisfy the needs of His people abundantly
God requires strict adherence without provision
God's provision is only spiritual, not physical
God's blessings depend on human works
questions.correctAnswer: God promises to satisfy the needs of His people abundantly
questions.explanation: Psalms 81:10 states, 'open thy mouth wide, and I will fill it,' indicating God's promise to abundantly provide for His people.

questions.question: What doctrine does Psalms 81:11 teach about human sin and divine patience?
options: Despite divine patience, people often reject God's voice
God immediately punishes every sin without delay
Human sin is insignificant to God
God forces obedience regardless of human will
questions.correctAnswer: Despite divine patience, people often reject God's voice
questions.explanation: Psalms 81:11 says, 'my people would not hearken to my voice; and Israel would none of me,' showing human rejection despite God's call.

questions.question: What doctrine does Psalms 81:12 teach about human free will and divine judgment?
options: God allows humans to follow their own desires as a form of judgment
God overrides human will forcing obedience
Human will is irrelevant to salvation
God's judgment is arbitrary and not connected to human choice
questions.correctAnswer: God allows humans to follow their own desires as a form of judgment
questions.explanation: Psalms 81:12 states, 'So I gave them up unto their own hearts' lust,' indicating God permits people to walk in their own counsel as judgment.

questions.question: Which divine attribute does Psalms 81:7 specifically demonstrate?
options: Providence
Omniscience
Justice
Longsuffering
questions.correctAnswer: Providence
questions.explanation: Psalms 81:7 reflects God's providential care in delivering Israel and testing them, demonstrating His providence over their circumstances.

questions.question: Which divine attribute does Psalms 81:14 specifically demonstrate?
options: Sovereignty
Immutability
Holiness
Mercy
questions.correctAnswer: Sovereignty
questions.explanation: In Psalms 81:14, God states He would have subdued their enemies and turned His hand against adversaries, showing His sovereign power over nations.

questions.question: How does Psalms 81:5 connect to the broader biblical theme of God's deliverance in redemptive history?
options: It prefigures God's deliverance of Israel from Egypt, foundational to salvation history
It describes a future deliverance unrelated to past events
It denies God's involvement in historical events
It emphasizes human effort over divine deliverance
questions.correctAnswer: It prefigures God's deliverance of Israel from Egypt, foundational to salvation history
questions.explanation: Psalms 81:5 recalls God's deliverance of Joseph's descendants from Egypt, a key event pointing to God's saving acts throughout Scripture.

questions.question: How does Psalms 81:16 contribute to the biblical narrative of God's provision and covenant faithfulness?
options: It affirms God's ongoing provision of sustenance symbolizing covenant blessing
It suggests God's provision is temporary and conditional
It denies God's involvement in daily needs
It shifts focus from covenant to legalism
questions.correctAnswer: It affirms God's ongoing provision of sustenance symbolizing covenant blessing
questions.explanation: Psalms 81:16 promises feeding with the finest wheat and honey from the rock, symbolizing God's faithful provision under His covenant.

questions.question: What combined doctrine do verses Psalms 81:8 and Psalms 81:9 teach about God's covenant demands and idolatry?
options: God commands exclusive worship and forbids idolatry as essential to covenant faithfulness
God allows worship of other gods alongside Him
Idolatry is tolerated if the heart is sincere
Covenant demands are secondary to ritual observance
questions.correctAnswer: God commands exclusive worship and forbids idolatry as essential to covenant faithfulness
questions.explanation: Psalms 81:8 calls Israel to hear God’s testimony, and 81:9 forbids strange gods, highlighting exclusive worship as covenant requirement.

questions.question: What combined doctrine do Psalms 81:13 and Psalms 81:14 teach about divine blessing contingent on human obedience?
options: Blessings and victory over enemies depend on Israel's obedience to God
Blessings are automatic regardless of human behavior
Obedience has no effect on divine blessing
Blessings come only through ritual sacrifice
questions.correctAnswer: Blessings and victory over enemies depend on Israel's obedience to God
questions.explanation: Verse 13 laments Israel's disobedience, and verse 14 promises subduing enemies if they obey, linking obedience to blessing.

questions.question: What combined doctrine do Psalms 81:6 and Psalms 81:7 teach about God's deliverance and human testing?
options: God both delivers His people from bondage and tests their faithfulness
God only delivers without testing
Testing replaces deliverance in God's plan
Deliverance is based solely on human merit
questions.correctAnswer: God both delivers His people from bondage and tests their faithfulness
questions.explanation: Verse 6 speaks of God's deliverance from burdens, while verse 7 references testing at Meribah, showing a pattern of deliverance and testing.

questions.question: Sceptics claim Psalms 81:11-12 shows God abandoning His people unjustly. What does Psalms 81:11-12 actually teach?
options: God permits people to follow their own lusts after they reject His voice
God capriciously abandons people without cause
God punishes people regardless of their choices
God's rejection is permanent and without hope
questions.correctAnswer: God permits people to follow their own lusts after they reject His voice
questions.explanation: These verses show God giving up people to their own desires after they refuse to listen, indicating judgment but not unjust abandonment.

questions.question: What doctrine does Psalms 81:1 teach about worship and God’s strength?
options: Joyful, loud worship recognizes God as the source of strength
Worship is a silent, private affair unrelated to divine strength
God's strength is hidden and not revealed through worship
Worship is merely a human duty without theological significance
questions.correctAnswer: Joyful, loud worship recognizes God as the source of strength
questions.explanation: Verse 1 commands singing aloud to God our strength, linking worship with acknowledgment of God's power.

questions.question: Which divine attribute does Psalms 81:16 specifically demonstrate?
options: Provision
Wrath
Transcendence
Immanence
questions.correctAnswer: Provision
questions.explanation: Verse 16 promises feeding with finest wheat and honey, demonstrating God's attribute of provision for His people.

questions.question: How does Psalms 81:3 contribute to the biblical narrative of appointed times and God's covenantal rhythms?
options: It emphasizes the importance of worship at divinely appointed festivals
It denies any special times for worship
It teaches worship should only be spontaneous and unregulated
It replaces festivals with individual prayer
questions.correctAnswer: It emphasizes the importance of worship at divinely appointed festivals
questions.explanation: Verse 3 calls to blow the trumpet at the new moon and solemn feast day, underlining God’s ordained times for worship.

questions.question: What combined doctrine do Psalms 81:4 and Psalms 81:5 teach about the role of divine law and historical testimony in Israel's identity?
options: God’s law and the memory of deliverance form the foundation of Israel’s covenant identity
Law and history are irrelevant to Israel’s faith
Israel’s identity is based solely on ethnic descent
Law replaces historical memory in defining Israel
questions.correctAnswer: God’s law and the memory of deliverance form the foundation of Israel’s covenant identity
questions.explanation: Verse 4 calls the feast a statute and law of God; verse 5 recalls deliverance from Egypt as testimony, linking law and history to covenant identity.
